steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Marriage patterns: the marriage rate in the UK has fallen to its lowest level since records began. First marriages have declined; the average age of first marriage has risen (30 for women, 32 for men). Reasons: secularisation (less religious pressure), changing attitudes (cohabitation is now socially acceptable), women's economic independence (no longer need to marry for financial security).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Divorce: the divorce rate increased dramatically after the 1969 Divorce Reform Act (made 'irretrievable breakdown' sufficient grounds). Currently about 42% of marriages end in divorce. Reasons: easier divorce laws, less stigma, women's financial independence, rising expectations of marriage (Giddens: confluent love - relationships only survive while both partners are satisfied).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cohabitation: living together without marriage. Has increased significantly - 20% of couples now cohabit. Some see it as a trial marriage; others see it as an alternative to marriage. Cohabiting couples have fewer legal rights than married couples. About half of cohabitations lead to marriage.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Birth rates: UK total fertility rate is about 1.6 children per woman (below replacement level of 2.1). Reasons: contraception, women's careers, later marriage, cost of raising children, changing values. Death rates: have fallen due to medical advances, better nutrition, improved sanitation. Life expectancy: 81 years (UK average).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why the divorce rate has increased in the UK since the 1960s. | Describe the demographic changes affecting UK families and assess their social implications. | Evaluate whether the decline of marriage is a problem for society.

steps.body: Divorce rate increased: 1969 Act + secularisation + less stigma + women's independence + higher expectations. UK fertility rate = 1.6 (below replacement 2.1). Ageing population = 19% over 65. Implications: pensions, healthcare, dependency ratio. Declining marriage: New Right = problem (instability). Feminism = progress (liberation). Postmodernism = choice (diversity).
